# OpenKache

A next-generation Rust SSD cache server — 10× cheaper and faster than Redis.

OpenKache uses SSD as primary storage instead of DRAM, reducing storage costs from ~$3-5/GB to ~$0.05-0.10/GB. It achieves competitive latency through SIMD-accelerated BCF53 breadcrumb filtering, QUIC multiplexed transport, and end-to-end encryption by default.

## Features

- **SSD-first architecture** — SSD as primary storage, not a secondary tier
- **SIMD-accelerated BCF53 filter** — 32+ million ops/sec per core, runtime SIMD dispatch (AVX-512, AVX2, SVE2, NEON)
- **QUIC transport** — Multiplexed streams, TLS 1.3 baked in, no head-of-line blocking
- **E2E encryption** — Zero-trust by default, configurable algorithm
- **Transparent compression** — zstd for large values
- **Multi-language SDKs** — Rust, TypeScript and JavaScript on Node.js, Bun, and Deno, and .NET; additional language packages are scaffolded for future Rust-backed bindings

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- Linux x86_64 or aarch64
- Rust toolchain
- NVMe SSD recommended

### Build

```bash
git clone https://github.com/openkache/openkache
cd openkache
cargo build --release
```

### Run benchmark

```bash
cargo run --package openkache --bin breadcrumb --release
```

### Use the Rust SDK

```rust
use openkache::prelude::*;

let client = OpenKacheClient::new("localhost:9000").await?;
client.set("mykey", b"myvalue").await?;
let value = client.get("mykey").await?;
```

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────┐         QUIC (UDP, TLS 1.3)         ┌──────────────────────┐
│  openkache-  │ ──────────────────────────────────▶ │     OpenKache        │
│  client      │   Multiplexed streams, 0-RTT        │  (single binary)     │
│  (Rust/.NET) │                                     │                      │
└──────────────┘                                     │  ┌────────────────┐  │
                                                     │  │ BCF53 Filter   │  │
┌──────────────┐                                     │  │ (SIMD, AVX2)   │  │
│  Any QUIC    │                                     │  ├────────────────┤  │
│  client      │                                     │  │ Compacting Slab│  │
└──────────────┘                                     │  │ (Hugepage/NUMA)│  │
                                                     │  ├────────────────┤  │
                                                     │  │ KV Engine      │  │
                                                     │  │ (SHA-256 keys) │  │
                                                     │  ├────────────────┤  │
                                                     │  │ SSD Engine     │  │
                                                     │  └────────────────┘  │
                                                     └──────────────────────┘
```

## Comparison

| | Redis | OpenKache |
|---|---|---|
| **Cost per GB** | DRAM (~$3–5/GB) | SSD (~$0.05–0.10/GB) |
| **P99 latency** | <1 ms | <1 ms |
| **Throughput** | ~100K ops/s (single node) | 1M+ ops/s (single node) |
| **Transport** | TCP (HOL blocking) | QUIC (TLS 1.3, multiplexed, 0-RTT) |
| **Security** | TLS optional, no E2E | E2E encrypted by default, zero trust |

## AI coding agents

OpenKache provides [`/llms.txt`](./llms.txt) and [`/llms-full.txt`](./llms-full.txt) for LLM-friendly documentation.

## Project status

| Component | Status |
|---|---|
| Memory allocators | Stable |
| Breadcrumb filter (BCF53) | Stable |
| QUIC client (Rust) | Stable |
| QUIC server | Preview — SSD-backed worker shards over multiplexed streams |
| .NET client | Stable |
| Clustering | Not started |

## Project structure

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `server/` | Core cache server (BCF53, allocators, types) |
| `clients/` | Implemented SDKs and thin-binding package scaffolds |
| `clients/rust/` | Rust client SDK over QUIC |
| `clients/typescript/` | TypeScript client backed by Rust through Node-API |
| `clients/dotnet/` | .NET / C# client SDK |
